Expert and highly experienced researcher and quantitative methodologist with 15+ years of demonstrated success specializing in measurement science and research methods. At [Amazon Web Services](https://aws.amazon.com/), I led end-to-end analytical and machine learning initiatives that shape product decisions, automate data pipelines, and improve operational efficiency. I served as the certification psychometrician for multiple AWS certification exams. My work bridges deep measurement and statistical expertise with scalable Python, R, SQL, and AWS infrastructure.

Before AWS, I was a tenured Associate Professor of Statistics, Measurement, and Evaluation in Education at the [University of Missouri](https://www.missouri.edu/) (2008–2022). My academic research focused on statistical modeling using large-scale assessment data, measurement, scale development, and program evaluation. I co-developed the Classroom Engagement Inventory and authored 50+ peer-reviewed papers, three books, and six book chapters.

## Core competencies

- **Quantitative Research Methods**: Survey design & distribution, experimental & quasi-experimental designs, causal inference, structural equation modeling, multilevel modeling, predictive modeling.
- **Measurement & Psychometrics**: Scale development & validation, measurement reliability, bias and fairness, job task analysis, standard setting, continuous improvement.
- **Programming & Data**: R, Python, SQL, Mplus, Winsteps, AWS infrastructure, automated data pipeline development, and data transformation.
- **Research & Product Impact**: End-to-end problem framing, technical writing, cross-functional collaboration, executive briefings, and leadership communication.

## Experience

### Amazon Web Services (AWS)
**Research Scientist/Certification Psychometrician** | 2022.6 – 2026.7

- Led psychometrics work for multiple AWS certification exams.
- Reviewed/Developed business requirements, designed research projects, proposed analytical methods, gathered and cleaned data, developed metrics, built statistical models, and wrote strategy and research papers.
- Proposed and implemented a design-based approach to headcount estimation to operate the AWS European Sovereign Cloud. Results were used by leadership to request/approve headcount.
- Developed metrics to measure teams’ operational load and efficiency. Metrics were integrated into internal dashboards and data pipelines.
- Built machine learning models of AWS service teams’ headcount and their operational load. Results were used to allocate headcount resources.
- Developed and automated processes to integrate various operational data sources and to generate data at different granularity levels for reporting and statistical analysis.
- Led a GenAI project for an internal AWS hackathon.
- Developed an AI workflow to automate and integrate processes for psychometrics work.
- Served as a regular reviewer for Amazon research conferences and AWS AI research proposals submitted by external researchers.
- Presented at national professional conferences
- Led and conducted the job task analysis; survey design, distribution, and analysis; and standard setting of the AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional certification.

### University of Missouri
**Tenured Associate Professor of Statistics, Measurement, and Evaluation in Education** | 2014 – 2022
**Assistant Professor** | 2008 – 2014

- Led the methodological design (e.g., replicated Latin Square Design, randomized controlled trials) and statistical implementation (e.g., power analysis, sampling, randomization, effect size estimation) of federal grants (NSF, IES) totaling over $10 million.
- Led and managed research groups of 20+ postdocs and graduate and undergraduate students in total.
- Led the development of the Classroom Engagement Inventory (350+ citations and adopted by 80+ scholars).

- Chaired 5 PhD committees and mentored 50+ doctoral and master’s students.
- Won multiple awards for research, service, mentoring, and teaching excellence.
- Served in leadership roles for national professional organizations.
- Served as advisor/consultant to research firms.

## Books

Two open-access books I've written for graduate-level quantitative methods courses.

### [Quantitative Foundations in Educational Research](/books/quant-foundations/)

A self-contained introduction to applied statistics for educational and social-science research: descriptive statistics, probability, sampling, inference, regression, and ANOVA. Developed for *ESC_PS 8850*, the master's-level methods course I taught at the University of Missouri. [Previous site →](https://zewang.netlify.app/books/quant-foundations/_book/) · [Lecture slides →](https://zewang.netlify.app/slides/quant-foundations/#1)

### [Structural Equation Modeling Using R and Mplus](/books/sem/)

A practical introduction to structural equation modeling with worked examples in both R (`lavaan`) and Mplus. Covers measurement models, path analysis, latent variable models, model fit, and multi-group / multilevel extensions. Built around *ESC_PS 9710*, a doctoral course I taught at the University of Missouri. [Previous site →](https://zewang.netlify.app/books/sem/_book/) · [Lecture slides →](https://zewang.netlify.app/slides/sem/#1)

## Selected projects

### [Flipped Mathematics Study](https://flippedmathstudy.net/)

NSF-funded research investigating how flipped-classroom instruction affects students' learning of mathematics across diverse classroom settings. **Award:** NSF DRL-1721025, $539,011 (2017–2021). PIs: Zandra de Araujo, Samuel J. Otten, Ze Wang, James Tarr.

### [Latinx Workers](http://nsfengineerstudy.org/)

NSF-funded collaborative research project, *Should I Stay or Should I Go? Understanding the Retention of Latinx in Engineering Jobs*. Designed and applied quantitative methods (survey design, multilevel modeling) to understand factors driving career persistence and attrition among Latinx engineers. **Award:** NSF 2000607, $1,546,428 (2020–2025). PIs: Lisa Y. Flores (University of Missouri), Rachel L. Navarro (University of North Dakota). Role: Key Personnel.
